subject: Atlas Health — regional lock proof & purge acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@atlashealth.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Atlas Health Security <security@atlashealth.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: evidence for region-bound storage + proof of deletion (Atlas Health)

David —

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. As part of our procurement security review we need a concise set of artifacts that show how Redwood will:

1) Guarantee Atlas Health tenant data remains resident in the US-East region (no cross-region replication or failover without explicit change control).
2) Demonstrate end-to-end deletion: when Atlas requests a tenant purge, what artifacts will you provide (timelines, logs, snapshots, and cryptographic checksums if applicable)?
3) Clarify backup/replication behavior: are backups replicated outside the pinned region, and if so under what conditions can we opt out?

Deliverables we want (target):
- High-level diagram of data flow and where each persistent copy lives.
- Playbook describing the tenant purge workflow and expected evidence (ops logs, snapshot metadata, wipe confirmation).
- SLA for purge completion (RPO/RTO expectations) and options for on-prem KMS or HSM key escrow.

Can you provide a one-week turnaround for the initial artifacts and a two-week window for an acceptance test run? We can coordinate with our infra/security engineering (I’ll loop them in after you share the draft).

Best,
Maya Singh
Head of Security Engineering
Atlas Health

(Attached: minimal checklist)
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@atlashealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: evidence for region-bound storage + proof of deletion (Atlas Health)

Maya —

Thanks — this is straightforward to scope. Attached is a draft playbook and a simplified dataflow diagram to start (redwood-erase-playbook-draft.pdf, atlas-dataflow-diagram.png). High-level answers below; we will expand into formal artifacts you can use for procurement and the acceptance test.

1) Region residency: For Redwood Dedicated we offer explicit region pinning per tenant. That means:
  - Primary serving cluster + persistent storage (object and block snapshots) are bound to the configured region (US-East).
  - Control plane metadata (non-customer data) may be in our control-plane region but is logically separated and never contains tenant content.
  - Failover to another region is only allowed via a documented change-control request that requires Atlas approval, and it is opt-in.

2) Deletion/purge: Our purge workflow produces the following artifacts which we can hand over:
  - Purge initiation audit entry (timestamp, request id, initiator).
  - Snapshot tombstone logs and snapshot manifest (indicates which snapshots were queued for deletion).
  - Storage-level deletion confirmations (object deletion events and eventual consistency confirmation).
  - Post-purge verification report (checksums absent, KV cache truncation confirmation, and list of the nodes involved).
  - Estimated SLAs: standard purge completes within 72 hours; expedited purge (paid) within 24 hours.

3) Backups & replication: Default Dedicated backups are region-local by policy. Cross-region replication occurs only under two scenarios:
  - Customer requests multi-region DR (explicit opt-in).
  - Exceptional codepath for hardware failure where we spin up a temporary cross-region copy under approval and notify the customer.

Next steps I propose: we’ll produce the formal playbook with logs and evidence samples within 5 business days. Can your team accept an in-person or remote acceptance run in the second week after that?

I’ll loop in Laura for the ops/verification artifacts and Priyom for the replication/backup clarifications.

Thanks,
David Kim
Director, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redwood-erase-playbook-draft.pdf, atlas-dataflow-diagram.png)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: evidence for region-bound storage + proof of deletion (Atlas Health)

David / Priyom / Ben —

Reviewing Maya’s checklist and David’s draft, I’m attaching an ops checklist excerpt that we can turn into the final evidence package. A few implementation notes we should commit to in the playbook so Atlas has clear acceptance criteria:

- Snapshots & object stores: we tag every snapshot with tenant-id, region, and snapshot-hash. For proof we will provide the snapshot manifest (json lines) and an audit log showing the manifest creation plus subsequent delete event.
- KV cache eviction: for models we keep ephemeral KV on serving nodes; purge will include an atomic kv-cache truncate event recorded in the node logs. We’ll include a sample truncated log line and a timeline.
- Disk wipe vs object delete: some storage backends only support object-level deletes. For those, we will provide replication sweep evidence and a glue script runbook that ensures objects are no longer reachable and are not restorable from any local backup.
- Backups: default is region-only snapshot retention for Dedicated. For Atlas we’ll add an explicit flag to the tenant config to disallow cross-region replication; this will be visible in the tenant manifest and we’ll show you the manifest entry as evidence.
- Cryptographic proof: we don’t currently provide cryptographic shred proofs, but we can provide SHA256 manifest diffs pre/post purge for verification.

I’m attaching the ops-checklist excerpt (ops-purge-checklist.txt) and a short sample manifest snippet in the playbook. Priyom — can you confirm the replication opt-out flag name and whether any edge-case DR automation still triggers replica creation? Ben — please prepare the sample node log lines for KV truncation.

Laura Bennett
Head of Operations, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: ops-purge-checklist.txt)

Subject: Re: Request: evidence for region-bound storage + proof of deletion (Atlas Health)

Maya —

Following up with the consolidated commitments from our ops and infra teams. Summary of what we will deliver for Atlas (target delivery: 2026-03-11):

1) Artifacts (PDF + raw samples):
  - Updated playbook (redwood-erase-playbook-final.pdf) with step-by-step purge workflow and acceptance checklist.
  - Dataflow diagram (atlas-dataflow-diagram.png) annotated with each persistent copy location.
  - Snapshot manifest sample and deletion event log (manifest_sample.jsonl, manifest_delete_log.txt).
  - KV cache truncate sample logs (kv_truncate_sample.log).

2) Acceptance test plan (two phases):
  - Dry-run (non-destructive): we’ll simulate purge actions and provide the manifests/logs listed above; Atlas security team validates artifacts.
  - Live purge (destructive): after Atlas signs off on the dry-run, we’ll perform a scheduled purge in a staging tenant and provide the full evidence bundle.

3) Timelines and SLAs:
  - Initial artifact package: 2 business days (by 2026-03-11).
  - Acceptance dry-run window: week of 2026-03-16.
  - Live purge (if opted in): within 72 hours of request, expedited option within 24 hours.

4) Options:
  - KMS: we support customer-managed KMS in Dedicated; we can include KMS key IDs in the manifest and a proof of key rotation for the purge.
  - Cross-region replication: disabled by default for your tenant; any cross-region action requires documented Atlas approval.

Please confirm the acceptance window and whether Atlas wants the dry-run to include the cryptographic manifest diffs (SHA256) or if the manifest + logs are sufficient. Once we get your confirmation I’ll send the formal package and Judy from our compliance team will join the dry-run kickoff.

Thanks,
David Kim
Director, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
(Attachments incoming: redwood-erase-playbook-final.pdf, manifest_sample.jsonl, kv_truncate_sample.log)
